clue.text: Lacking members to back the Church, it's unpleasant

indicators.note: the limbless word comes behind, backing up, the church abbreviation

parts.note: members are limbs, so lacking them is being without arms

explanation.surface: A grumble about a congregation too thin to support its church, and how disagreeable that is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' means limbs here, not people who belong to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking any appeal or attractiveness is disagreeable, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Fish scoffing brilliant apple

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat up, so the fish word swallows the other word inside it

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
star as an adjective means outstanding, brilliant

explanation.surface: A greedy fish gobbling down a splendid apple.
explanation.definitionFit: The costard is an old English variety of large cooking apple.

clue.text: Bristle, as part of law nullified

indicators.note: the letters sought form a part of the run of letters in the next two words

explanation.surface: A legal note on a provision that has been cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically, the fine bristle on an ear of barley or other grass is called by this name.

clue.text: 1320 yards before dog catches tail of athletic dairy animal

indicators.note: the yardage piece comes in front of the dog piece

parts.note: 1320 yards is three quarters of a mile, so three of the four letters of MILE

indicators.note: the dog word grabs a letter and holds it inside

parts.note: the chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here of athletic

explanation.surface: A distance run, then a dog snapping at a runner's heels, all leading to a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: '1320 yards' is three quarters of a mile, so take three quarters of the word MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow kept for milk is a dairy animal; figuratively it is a ready source of easy money.

clue.text: Time to bag ten thousand for a start, as bonus

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the time word holds the others inside

parts.note: an era is a period of time
X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: a start of a word is its opening letter, here of thousand

explanation.surface: An era of time pocketing ten thousand as a starting bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional, given over and above what is due, is a bonus.

clue.text: Flat replacement for middleweight?

parts.note: a reserve wheel carried in case of a puncture, and jokingly a roll of fat around the waist of someone heavy in the middle

explanation.surface: A query about substituting one boxer in a weight class for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is a punctured wheel, and 'middleweight' is someone carrying weight around the middle, not a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a reserve wheel for punctures and, colloquially, a bulge of flab at the waist.

clue.text: Constant function for loop

parts.note: pi is the mathematical constant relating circumference to diameter
cot is the cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Maths jargon for a constant function used in a programming loop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loop' looks like computing, but it is a decorative loop of thread.
explanation.definitionFit: In lace and embroidery this word names one of the small decorative loops along an edge.

clue.text: Unit of pressure drawing up resin and plant fluid

indicators.note: in a down entry, drawing up means the letters are read bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: lac is a resinous substance secreted by insects
sap is the fluid circulating in plants

explanation.surface: Pressure drawing resin and sap up through a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of pressure, one newton per square metre, is named after Blaise Pascal.

clue.text: Master cracking a clue that's cryptic on time for artist

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed after, so the time letter follows
the master word breaks into the jumbled letters, sitting inside them
cryptic means puzzling or obscure, so the letters of a clue are rearranged

parts.note: a demon at something is an expert, a master of it

explanation.surface: An expert solver cracking a cryptic clue in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' looks like an old master, but it means DEMON, an ace; it goes inside CLAUE, from 'cryptic' working on A CLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Impressionist painter of the water lilies is a celebrated artist.

clue.text: Smack, then batter Chinese puzzle

parts.note: a smack is a taste or flavour, as is a tang
to ram is to strike repeatedly, to batter

explanation.surface: A violent sequence: a slap, then a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' is a flavour, not a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: The dissection puzzle of seven flat pieces forming shapes originated in China.

clue.text: Sleeveless garment, way to keep warmer?

indicators.note: the way abbreviation keeps the other word held inside it

parts.note: ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way
an ingle is a fireside or hearth, something that warms

explanation.surface: A vest without sleeves, suggested as a way of keeping someone warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmer' is a noun, a hearth, not a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest without arms, as worn by athletes, is a sleeveless garment.

clue.text: Pass a black spot

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: Passing on a black spot, as if refusing pirate's doom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' is the verb of declining to vote or act.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline to vote or take part, as in a ballot, is to pass.

clue.text: Leaders in all administrative regions generally hapless — oh no!

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A lament that regional government is broadly hopeless everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of dismay or frustration, interjections used when something goes wrong.

clue.text: US policies once implicating military leader in heinous crimes, no?

indicators.note: the commander word sits inside the jumbled letters
heinous means wicked, so the letters of crimes and no are twisted out of shape

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander

explanation.surface: A query whether a general was implicated in wicked crimes under a past US administration.
explanation.definitionFit: The supply-side economic programme of the 1980s US president is a past American set of policies.

clue.text: Pope, a tragic youth bearing cross

indicators.note: the youth's name carries the cross letter inside it

parts.note: Leander, in Greek myth, drowned swimming the Hellespont to his lover Hero
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A doomed young man carrying a crucifix, with a pope looming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope' could suggest the poet, but here it means a pontiff: several popes took this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight pontiffs have reigned under this name, so it identifies a pope.

clue.text: Shrew quick to find insect

parts.note: a shrew is a scolding woman, a dragon
fly in British slang means sharp, quick-witted

explanation.surface: A small mammal speedy enough to find an insect to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' is a nagging woman, not the animal; 'fly' is British slang for sharp-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-bodied darting creature with two pairs of wings is an insect.

clue.text: International communication process fails, having called for investment?

indicators.note: investment is enclosing, so the telephoned word is put inside
to process material is to work it over, so the letters of fails are rearranged

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A cross-border messaging system breaks down, and someone has called for money to be put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' looks financial, but it is the old sense of clothing or enclosing; 'process' scrambles the fodder to FLAIS.
explanation.definitionFit: This blend of French and English words is jokingly a mixed language across nations.

clue.text: Announcement of PM's successor: a Muslim ruler

parts.note: I'm, as in introducing oneself, is an announcement
the hours after noon, p.m., are followed by those before noon, a.m.

explanation.surface: A new Prime Minister's successor declared, and a Muslim leader named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM's successor' looks political, but after p.m. comes a.m. on the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An Islamic leader, whether of prayers in a mosque or of a community, holds this title.

clue.text: Caterpillar in underground stem touring borders in hedgerow

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the stem word surrounds the edge letters

parts.note: a corm is a swollen underground plant stem, like a crocus bulb

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its first and last letters, here of hedgerow

explanation.surface: A caterpillar crawls inside a bulb going around the edge of a hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: The larva of the geometrid moth, which loops as it moves, is a caterpillar.

clue.text: Chestnut tree's centre hollowed out

indicators.note: hollowing out the centre removes the middle letter of the tree

parts.note: the rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree

explanation.surface: A chestnut tree with its trunk hollowed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chestnut' looks like the tree, but it is a horse colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse whose coat is reddish-brown mixed with white hairs is described with this colour term, like a chestnut.

clue.text: Little time hiding rings — like diamonds?

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so the defeat word surrounds the time word

parts.note: a hiding is a thrashing, a rout
sec, short for second, is a little time

explanation.surface: A brief moment hiding wedding rings, which may hold diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' is a heavy defeat, not concealment; 'rings' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of faceting with a flat base and triangular facets is used for some cut gems.

clue.text: Range — a pound figures

parts.note: a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen
nines are numerals, figures

explanation.surface: A price range listed as a pound and some numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is an enclosure, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: The chain of mountains running down the length of Italy is a range.

clue.text: Man passing current through fuse

indicators.note: the current letter runs through, inside, the fuse word

parts.note: to solder is to fuse metal
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An electrician sending a current through a fuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A man in the ranks of an army, or a person who serves in one, is a soldier.

clue.text: General occupying filthy home that's cold and damp

indicators.note: the general occupies, sits inside, the dirty home

parts.note: a sty, or pigsty, is a filthy dwelling
Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the US Civil War

explanation.surface: A general billeted in a squalid, chilly, damp house.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather of mixed rain and snow is chilly and wet.

clue.text: Focus attention on insignificant boxing prize

indicators.note: to box is to enclose, so the minor word encloses the prize word

parts.note: slight means minor, insignificant
a pot is a trophy or prize

explanation.surface: Drawing attention to a minor boxing trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport, but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick out for public notice, as with a stage lamp, is to direct attention on something.

clue.text: Big pussycat good to break up row

indicators.note: the good letter breaks the row word apart, sitting inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A large cat that is good at breaking up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped Asian big cat is jokingly a large pussycat.

clue.text: House call that comes after golf

definitions.meaning: a building providing rooms for guests; to house is to lodge
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for H follows the one for G, Golf

explanation.surface: A clubhouse visit after a round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel houses guests, and in radio spelling its name is the call for the letter after G.

clue.text: Fancy man in unpredictable race

indicators.note: the man word goes inside the jumbled letters
an unpredictable arrangement scrambles the letters of race

parts.note: him stands for a man

explanation.surface: A fancied runner in a race that could go any way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is a noun, an illusion, not the verb of backing a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild illusion or fantastic notion is a fancy, as is a mythical monster of mixed parts.

clue.text: Italian food that's cold then hot in cooking, not ok to change

indicators.note: the tap letters go inside the rearranged letters
the remaining letters change their order
not ok means the letters of ok are removed from cooking

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Cooking an Italian dish, alternating cold and hot, which goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges what is left, COING, into GNOCI before the tap letters go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Small potato or semolina dumplings are a dish from Italy.

clue.text: Pass unfriendly contracts

indicators.note: the cool word contracts, shrinking by losing one letter

parts.note: cool means aloof, unfriendly

explanation.surface: A hostile party passing on some deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' is a verb, shrinks, not agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain pass or saddle between peaks has this geographical name.

clue.text: Twenty-fifth experiment, perhaps, making one irritable?

parts.note: a test is an experiment
Y is the 25th letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The twenty-fifth trial in a series, enough to make anyone cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Twenty-fifth experiment' as a test labelled with the 25th letter, so the letter follows the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easily annoyed, short-tempered, is a near synonym of touchy.

clue.text: Biker initially seen cycling ahead of walker

indicators.note: the two first letters come in front of the walker
initially picks out the first letters of seen and cycling

parts.note: a rambler is someone who walks in the countryside

explanation.surface: A motorcyclist spotted riding ahead of a hiker.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on a motorcycle built for rough cross-country racing is called this.
